A model of bile acid transport in hepatocytes, fitted to two experimental conditions from many
starts and profiled. The [guide](guide-model.html) covers each step on a larger model.

```{r setup}
```

## Data and conditions

Bile acid in buffer and cells, measured with closed and opened tight junctions, one data set per
[condition]{#def-condition}. A condition, here `closed` or `open`, is one experimental setting with
own data and own model parameters.

```{r data}
```

```{r}
plot(data)
```

## Model definition

Bile acid moves from the buffer into the cells, from the cells into buffer or canaliculi, and
from the canaliculi back into the buffer.

```{r reactions}
```

`odemodel()` generates C++ code for ODE and sensitivities, `Xs()` makes the
[prediction function]{#def-prdfn} (`prdfn`) from parameters to trajectories, `Y()` the
[observation function]{#def-obsfn} (`obsfn`) from trajectories to observables: cells and canaliculi are
measured together, both observables with scale `s`.
Expressions follow the
[expression language of cppDE](https://dmodverse.github.io/cppDE/reference/expressions.html),
including switches such as `piecewise()`.

```{r model}
```

`P()` is a [parameter transformation]{#def-parfn} (`parfn`). It maps the
[outer parameters]{#def-outer-parameters}, which the optimizer sees (`K_IMPORT`, `S`, ... on log10
scale), to the [inner parameters]{#def-inner-parameters} of ODE and observables in one condition
(`k_import`, `s`, ...), with an empty buffer at the start.
`branch()` makes one transformation per condition, open junctions with a separate reflux rate
`K_REFLUX_OPEN`. All three function objects compile into one shared object.

```{r trafo}
```

`+` and `branch()` join conditions; `*` composes function objects by the chain rule, so every
call returns values with their derivatives in the outer parameters, the objective value, gradient
and Hessian.

## Likelihood, prior and fit

`normL2()` returns an [objective function]{#def-objfn} (`objfn`), here $-2 \log L$ of the data; a
weak prior from `constraintL2()` keeps parameters the data do not determine finite, and the sum is
$-2 \log$ of the posterior.

```{r objective}
```

`trust()` is a trust-region fit from one start; `mstrust()` runs it from 50 random starts around
`pouter`, standard deviation 4 on log10 scale ([options](guide-optimization.html)).

```{r fit, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
saved <- stored("results/dMod2.rds", "results/dMod2.R", envir = new.env())
fits <- saved$fits
profiles <- saved$profiles
```

`plotValues()` sorts the fits by value; a plateau at the lowest value indicates the global
optimum.

```{r}
plotValues(fits)
```

`as.parvec()` takes the best fit.

```{r best}
```

```{r}
fits[1, c("value", "converged", "iterations")]
best
plot((g * x * p)(seq(0, 50, length.out = 200), best, deriv = FALSE), data)
```

## Profile likelihood

`profile()` moves each parameter away from the optimum, the others following the path on which
they stay optimal. A confidence
interval ends where the profile crosses the threshold.

```{r profile, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plotProfile(profiles, mode == "data")
confint(profiles, val.column = "data")
```

`S`, `TCA_CELL` and `TCA_CANA` are flat, a structural non-identifiability: smaller initial
amounts compensate a larger scale. [Symmetries](guide-symmetries.html) finds and removes it
systematically; the [bile acid project](bileAcidTransport.html) fixes the scale, starts the
canaliculi in steady state and goes on to prediction bands. `K_EXPORT_SINUS` and `K_REFLUX_OPEN`
are bounded on one side only, a practical non-identifiability.
